It re-sends the original\\'s title and description, and it reasons only about the original\\'s time window. A replay is read-only: it cannot be steered, forked or mitigated, and it changes nothing in the customer\\'s systems. {"id": "4d2d99fd-944a-40e3-951f-72117eadced3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You may not need a separate baseline. A replay re-runs a finished investigation with your current configuration, and the docs say the replay and its original are both reviewed automatically. So the old run can get a score now, even though it was never scored when it ran.

**How to run the comparison**
1. Pick a few completed investigations that ran under the old prompt. Choose ones that cover different incident types.
2. Replay each one. This re-sends the original title and description over the original time window. A replay is read-only and changes nothing in your systems. You can add a note such as "new prompt v2".
3. Compare each pair of runs. The comparison shows:
   - grader score, with a pass or fail verdict per criterion
   - root cause found
   - time to root cause
   - tools and skills used

**Limits on the evidence**
- **Prompt vs. other changes:** The replay uses your agent's skills, memory and instructions as they are now. If anything besides the prompt changed since the original run, it can affect the result. Keep the prompt as the only variable if you can.
- **Live data:** Replays query your live environment. Logs and metrics from the original incident may be gone, especially past the 14-day retention window, so a replay can see less data than the original did.
- **Sample size:** One pair proves little. A handful of replays, with a consistent grade change and faster time to root cause, makes a stronger case.
- **One replay at a time:** You can only run one replay of a given investigation at a time. You can replay the same one more than once and compare any two runs.
- **Grader rubric:** The grader applies the same criteria to both runs, which keeps the comparison fair. It's still an automated score, so spot-check the root causes yourself.

If you give me investigation IDs, I can check which ones already have a review. I can then start replays for you. I'll show you the exact prompt and time window before I start anything.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
